editorial:
Imagine two guys who have absolutely nothing left to lose. You have Tae-sik, a middle-aged man who has hit rock bottom, and Sang-hwan, a rebellious kid with a lot of anger. They are both lost in life and feel like the world has given up on them. When they discover boxing, it is not just about hitting someone in the face; it is about finding a reason to wake up in the morning. The movie feels like a gritty underdog story that hits you right in the heart, mixing sad moments with a lot of raw energy.

The acting is top-notch and makes you really root for these two unlikely fighters. The fight scenes are punchy and realistic, so you feel every hit. While the middle part slows down a bit, the emotional payoff at the end is totally worth it. If you love stories about people fighting their way out of a hole, you need to see this.
endingExplained: In the final match, the two men push themselves to their absolute limits. It is not about who wins the trophy, but about proving they can survive. After a brutal fight, they both find a sense of peace and mutual respect. They realize that the struggle was the actual victory. The movie ends with them having regained their dignity and a new hope for their futures, showing that it is never too late to start over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves sports dramas and stories about redemption.
